commit.message:
Add multi-set draft: select the set filling each booster (#7964)

* Added support for selecting sets in a draft

* Address final review-impl findings on the multi-set merge

Two gaps the post-merge review found, both in code this merge introduced:

- `pack_pick_steps` shipped with no test at the seam that computes it. The
  only coverage was a frontend component test fed a hand-built literal, so
  the `div_ceil` derivation never ran through `filter_for_player` — and the
  case the field exists for (a CommanderDraft whose boosters differ in size)
  was untested. Adds an engine test asserting [10, 7, 8] for pack sizes
  [20, 14, 16] at two cards per step, which no competing implementation
  reproduces: publishing `pack_sizes` gives the card counts, and broadcasting
  the scalar `pick_steps_per_pack` gives [7, 7, 7]. Verified discriminating —
  the revert-probe reds it at [10, 10, 10].

- `concession_set_code` contradicted CR 903.13e, which grants on what the
  draft CONTAINED rather than on the draft being exclusively one set: a mixed
  CMM+CLB Commander draft should concede both The Prismatic Piper and
  Faceless One. `DraftSetConcessions` holds a single filler and cannot express
  the union without an engine-crate change, so the restrictive answer stands
  for now. Documents the gap against the rule text and pins both sides of the
  all-equal guard, including the repeated-code case that proves the guard
  reads set identity rather than sequence length. Unreachable in production:
  `create_multiplayer_draft` always builds `DraftSource::single_set`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Carry CR 903.13 draft concessions as a per-set union

Completes the multi-set draft work and makes the Commander Draft
deck-construction concessions rules-correct for a draft whose boosters
came from several sets.

CR 903.13e/f state each concession as an independent containment
condition ("If the draft contained draft boosters from ..."), so a draft
that opened Commander Masters and Battle for Baldur's Gate boosters
satisfies two of them: it concedes The Prismatic Piper AND Faceless One,
and keeps CR 903.13f(3)'s partner grant because it contained Commander
Masters. The previous model could name only one set and answered with no
concession at all, which multi-set selection made reachable.

Engine:
- DraftSetConcessions.filler becomes fillers, plus a union that does not
  stack either axis: a repeated filler name keeps the larger cap
  (CR 903.13e grants "up to two" once per name), and the CR 903.13f(3)
  colour bound takes the widest any contained set grants.
- draft_set_concessions_for is the new union authority, driven by the
  concession table rather than the caller's sequence, so order,
  repetition, casing and unnamed neighbours cannot move the answer.

Carried to the deck-validation boundary:
- draft_set_code becomes draft_set_codes on DeckCompatibilityRequest,
  DeckList, validate_name_deck_for_format_full and the player/spectator
  views; validate_limited_deck caps each grant on its own name.
- One shared deserializer accepts the array, the legacy single string and
  null, so stored decks and pre-multi-set payloads restore correctly.

Frontend renders one grant line per filler and passes the full code list
to commanderPartnerCandidates. DRAFT_PROTOCOL_VERSION 19 -> 20: this is a
rename in both directions, and silently losing a grant the rules make is
the defect the bump exists to refuse.

Also includes the remaining multi-set draft work from concurrent sessions
(set selection UI, pack-order persistence, pod wire guards, i18n), which
shares several files with the above and could not be split by pathspec.

Verified: cargo fmt/clippy clean; engine lib 19813 and integration 5586
tests; draft-core, server-core, draft-wasm, engine-wasm 689 tests;
frontend type-check and affected suites. WASM bundles rebuilt and the
full Quick Draft flow driven end to end in a browser through to a running
match, which the compiled test suites do not cover.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(PR-7964): port draft view fixture across pack metadata

* fix(PR-7964): cap retained draft pack selections

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: matthewevans <matthewevans@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
feat(draft): add Commander Draft (CR 903.13) (#7957)

Commander Draft as a first-class format: a pod drafts, designates its
commanders, and launches the multiplayer Commander game it earned.

Engine and draft-core:
  - `GameFormat::CommanderDraft` with a typed deck-size rule, replacing
    the per-format literals; CR 903.13f routes deck construction through
    CR 903.5, so CR 903.3 commander eligibility applies unchanged.
  - `DraftProcedure` becomes the single authority for per-kind axes, and
    a new `PackDistribution` is an E0004 rather than a silent `else`.
  - The two-card pick step (CR 903.13b), the pod seat floor (CR 903.13a
    + CR 800.1), and the commander designation floor (CR 903.3).
  - The CMM partner grant (CR 702.124g/h) and singleton suppression on
    the summary path.

Wire: Commander Draft is reachable across both encodings, and the deck
submission carries its commander designation. `validateSubmitDeck` is
the single authority for that message, enforcing the idempotency
`submissionId` and the CR 903.3 `commanders` field together.

Client: a reachable entry point, pod lobby, two-card pick UI, commander
panel, and a legality-honest refusal when a pod has not earned its
launch. Strings for all seven locales.

Protocol bumps this change owes: full-game 41 -> 42, P2P wire 31 -> 32,
lobby 1 -> 2, draft 14 -> 18.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01BT4WMBPwomvbddBcvTTG83

Co-authored-by: matthewevans <matthewevans@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
feat(draft,client): filter the limited build screen pool (#7507) (#7546)

* feat(draft,client): filter the limited build screen pool (#7507)

The build screen rendered the drafted pool as one flat grid; the only
search box on the screen narrows the addable basics, not the pool. On a
45-card pool, "show me my creatures" meant scanning by eye.

Every filter axis keys on the ENGINE's own pool classification, so the
display never re-derives a game category from raw card fields (the #6663
finding): type and color chips come from the existing
`DraftPoolGroups::from_pool` groups, and rarity joins them as the fourth
engine-owned axis (`rarity_groups`, standard four buckets plus a
`RarityOther` collector for "special"/"bonus" — kept a raw string on the
instance, bucketed by the engine). The chips one axis offers are exactly
the groups the engine delivered for this pool, in engine order.

Within an axis selections OR, across axes they AND, and a name query
mirrors the existing addable-cards box (display-layer, per the issue).
Duplicate copies stay covered: group entries collapse by name, so the
lookup keys on the engine's own collapse key rather than the single
representative instance id.

Issue #7507's open questions, settled here as: rarity engine-side (Q1),
name search display-side (Q2), build screen only (Q3) — `PoolPanel`
still sorts, now with `rarity_groups` available for a later axis.

Counter-probes: with the wiring bypassed, both component rows fail; the
helper rows discriminate as pure-function tests. Rust: rarity bucketing
and the serde wire contract are pinned in draft-core.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(PR-7546): key filter membership on instance ids, meet the 44pt floor

Review round 1. The filter's lookup was name-keyed, but same-name instances
can sit in different groups on one axis (a reprint at a different rarity):
one copy's classification overwrote the other's and the wrong card was
hidden. `DraftPoolEntry` now carries `instance_ids` — every collapsed
copy's id, filled by `sorted_entries` — and the client indexes each axis by
instance id. The field is compiler-guarded at every construction site on
both sides (one Rust literal, the TS fixtures were forced by `tsc`).

Regressions: draft-core pins that a common/rare same-name pair lands in two
rarity groups each addressing exactly its own copy (while their shared type
group addresses both); the client rows select each copy by ITS rarity.
Counter-probe: with the lookup reverted to name-keyed, 5 rows fail.

Chips get the repository's 44pt coarse-pointer floor with the same desktop
relaxation as the CubeSetupPanel inputs alongside (`min-h-[44px] ...
sm:min-h-0`).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(PR-7546): move pool filtering into the engine, complete the wire transition

Review round 2. The filtering authority now lives in draft-core:
`PoolFilter` is the typed contract (what the display asks for) and
`filter_pool_listing` decides which instances match — OR within an axis,
AND across axes, case-insensitive name query, instance-keyed membership.
A stateless draft-wasm export carries it to the client (usable by P2P
guests; no session required); the React screen keeps only presentation
state (pressed chips, query text) and renders exactly the returned ids,
falling back to the UNFILTERED listing if the engine call fails rather
than interpreting the data itself. The former client-side filter logic is
deleted; its discriminating tests (same-name/different-rarity included)
moved to draft-core.

Wire transition: `DRAFT_PROTOCOL_VERSION` 10 → 11 (guests hard-reject
mismatched hosts). For persisted/replayed v10 messages, serde defaults on
`rarity_groups`/`instance_ids` keep old JSON deserializing and
`normalizeDraftPlayerView` upgrades the shape: missing rarity axis becomes
empty, an old entry's `instance_ids` becomes its representative id — the
one instance the v10 shape can address; a multi-copy entry's other ids
were never serialized, and re-deriving them would make the normalizer a
second classification authority. Both shapes are pinned in
draftProtocol.test.ts; the gzip round-trip fixture is lifted to v11.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(PR-7546): classify inside the filter authority, announce a failed filter

Review round 3. The filter no longer consults wire-delivered groups at
all: `filter_pool_listing(listing, filter)` classifies each instance with
the same per-card classifiers the group builder uses. That removes the
legacy hazard at its root — a persisted/replayed v10 view whose collapsed
`count: 2` entries carry no instance ids cannot drop a copy, because the
groups are not an input; classification is total (every axis has a
residual bucket), so an unclassifiable listing entry cannot exist. The
groups stay what they already were elsewhere: presentation payload (chip
derivation, PoolPanel sorting). Regressions: a two-copy listing passes a
constrained type and rarity axis in full (`a_legacy_view_filters_every_
collapsed_copy`); the former stale-stray row now pins totality instead.

A failed engine round trip is no longer silent: the screen keeps the
unfiltered fallback but shows an alert beside the controls ("Filters are
unavailable right now — showing all cards", all 7 locales), cleared on
the next successful call. Counter-probe: with the flag write removed, the
new component row fails at the missing alert.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(PR-7546): filter by every type a card carries, harden the chip floor

Review round 4. CR 205.2a: card types are multi-valued, but the filter
matched only the exclusive presentation bucket — an Artifact Creature was
unreachable through the Artifact selection. `type_memberships` is now the
filtering membership (every bucket the card belongs to, engine order); the
exclusive `type_group` becomes its first element, so the sorted display
and the filter cannot drift. `DraftPoolGroups.type_filter_options` carries
the engine-owned option list (all memberships present in the pool), so a
pool of Artifact Creatures offers BOTH chips; legacy views carry none and
the control falls back to their exclusive buckets. Regressions: Artifact
Creature / Enchantment Creature / Artifact Land selections, the option
list, and the unchanged exclusive display shape. Counter-probe: with the
filter reverted to the exclusive bucket, the row fails at
`left: ["Tomb"]`.

Chips keep the 44px floor in BOTH dimensions and relax it only for fine
pointers (`pointer-fine:`), never at a viewport breakpoint; a component
row pins both floors and the absence of the breakpoint relaxation.

Known remainder, stated: the color axis stays bucket-exact — unlike the
type axis it offers an explicit Multicolor option, so every card remains
reachable through some chip; widening it to per-color membership would
change the meaning of an existing control rather than fix a reachability
hole.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(PR-7546): a card's colors are memberships too, and cite CR 205.2b

Colors are multi-valued exactly like types (CR 105.2: "an object can be
one or more of the five colors") — leaving the color axis bucket-exact
after fixing the type axis repeated the same defect one axis over. A
white-blue card is now reached by the White chip AND the Blue chip AND
Multicolor (CR 105.2b); Colorless covers CR 105.2c. Same shape as the
type fix: `color_memberships` is the filtering membership,
`color_filter_options` the engine-owned option list, the exclusive
`color_groups` stays the sorted display. Regressions mirror the type
rows; counter-probe: reverted to the exclusive bucket, the row fails at
`left: ["Pacifism"]` (the White selection loses the white-blue card).

Also corrects round 4's citation: multi-type membership is CR 205.2b
("satisfy the criteria for any effect that applies to any of their card
types"), not CR 205.2a (the type list).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(PR-7546): rebuild a legacy view's filter options through the engine

Review round 5. A legacy (pre-v11) view's controls fell back to the
exclusive presentation buckets — which cannot offer an Artifact Creature's
Artifact chip or a multicolored card's per-color chips even though the
filter itself would match them. The fallback is deleted: draft-core gains

feat(draft,client): filter the limited build screen pool (#7507) (#7546)

* feat(draft,client): filter the limited build screen pool (#7507)

The build screen rendered the drafted pool as one flat grid; the only
search box on the screen narrows the addable basics, not the pool. On a
45-card pool, "show me my creatures" meant scanning by eye.

Every filter axis keys on the ENGINE's own pool classification, so the
display never re-derives a game category from raw card fields (the #6663
finding): type and color chips come from the existing
`DraftPoolGroups::from_pool` groups, and rarity joins them as the fourth
engine-owned axis (`rarity_groups`, standard four buckets plus a
`RarityOther` collector for "special"/"bonus" — kept a raw string on the
instance, bucketed by the engine). The chips one axis offers are exactly
the groups the engine delivered for this pool, in engine order.

Within an axis selections OR, across axes they AND, and a name query
mirrors the existing addable-cards box (display-layer, per the issue).
Duplicate copies stay covered: group entries collapse by name, so the
lookup keys on the engine's own collapse key rather than the single
representative instance id.

Issue #7507's open questions, settled here as: rarity engine-side (Q1),
name search display-side (Q2), build screen only (Q3) — `PoolPanel`
still sorts, now with `rarity_groups` available for a later axis.

Counter-probes: with the wiring bypassed, both component rows fail; the
helper rows discriminate as pure-function tests. Rust: rarity bucketing
and the serde wire contract are pinned in draft-core.

* fix(PR-7546): key filter membership on instance ids, meet the 44pt floor

Review round 1. The filter's lookup was name-keyed, but same-name instances
can sit in different groups on one axis (a reprint at a different rarity):
one copy's classification overwrote the other's and the wrong card was
hidden. `DraftPoolEntry` now carries `instance_ids` — every collapsed
copy's id, filled by `sorted_entries` — and the client indexes each axis by
instance id. The field is compiler-guarded at every construction site on
both sides (one Rust literal, the TS fixtures were forced by `tsc`).

Regressions: draft-core pins that a common/rare same-name pair lands in two
rarity groups each addressing exactly its own copy (while their shared type
group addresses both); the client rows select each copy by ITS rarity.
Counter-probe: with the lookup reverted to name-keyed, 5 rows fail.

Chips get the repository's 44pt coarse-pointer floor with the same desktop
relaxation as the CubeSetupPanel inputs alongside (`min-h-[44px] ...
sm:min-h-0`).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(PR-7546): move pool filtering into the engine, complete the wire transition

Review round 2. The filtering authority now lives in draft-core:
`PoolFilter` is the typed contract (what the display asks for) and
`filter_pool_listing` decides which instances match — OR within an axis,
AND across axes, case-insensitive name query, instance-keyed membership.
A stateless draft-wasm export carries it to the client (usable by P2P
guests; no session required); the React screen keeps only presentation
state (pressed chips, query text) and renders exactly the returned ids,
falling back to the UNFILTERED listing if the engine call fails rather
than interpreting the data itself. The former client-side filter logic is
deleted; its discriminating tests (same-name/different-rarity included)
moved to draft-core.

Wire transition: `DRAFT_PROTOCOL_VERSION` 10 → 11 (guests hard-reject
mismatched hosts). For persisted/replayed v10 messages, serde defaults on
`rarity_groups`/`instance_ids` keep old JSON deserializing and
`normalizeDraftPlayerView` upgrades the shape: missing rarity axis becomes
empty, an old entry's `instance_ids` becomes its representative id — the
one instance the v10 shape can address; a multi-copy entry's other ids
were never serialized, and re-deriving them would make the normalizer a
second classification authority. Both shapes are pinned in
draftProtocol.test.ts; the gzip round-trip fixture is lifted to v11.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(PR-7546): classify inside the filter authority, announce a failed filter

Review round 3. The filter no longer consults wire-delivered groups at
all: `filter_pool_listing(listing, filter)` classifies each instance with
the same per-card classifiers the group builder uses. That removes the
legacy hazard at its root — a persisted/replayed v10 view whose collapsed
`count: 2` entries carry no instance ids cannot drop a copy, because the
groups are not an input; classification is total (every axis has a
residual bucket), so an unclassifiable listing entry cannot exist. The
groups stay what they already were elsewhere: presentation payload (chip
derivation, PoolPanel sorting). Regressions: a two-copy listing passes a
constrained type and rarity axis in full (`a_legacy_view_filters_every_
collapsed_copy`); the former stale-stray row now pins totality instead.

A failed engine round trip is no longer silent: the screen keeps the
unfiltered fallback but shows an alert beside the controls ("Filters are
unavailable right now — showing all cards", all 7 locales), cleared on
the next successful call. Counter-probe: with the flag write removed, the
new component row fails at the missing alert.

* fix(PR-7546): filter by every type a card carries, harden the chip floor

Review round 4. CR 205.2a: card types are multi-valued, but the filter

Creature / Enchantment Creature / Artifact Land selections, the option

filter reverted to the exclusive bucket, the row fails at

Chips keep the 44px floor in BOTH dimensions and relax it only for fine
pointers (`pointer-fine:`), never at a viewport breakpoint; a component
row pins both floors and the absence of the breakpoint relaxation.

Known remainder, stated: the color axis stays bucket-exact — unlike the
type axis it offers an explicit Multicolor option, so every card remains
reachable through some chip; widening it to per-color membership would
change the meaning of an existing control rather than fix a reachability
hole.
